*   **Performance:** The method reduces cache misses by ensuring spatially adjacent voxels are stored contiguously in memory [S1].

The claim states that the method reduces cache misses by ensuring spatially adjacent voxels are stored contiguously. The evidence explicitly states in Section 4.3.4 that 'To reduce cache misses, the volume is decomposed in small blocks... where the bits of the coordinates are interleaved'. The interleaving scheme described (grouping higher bits by dimension and interleaving lower bits) is a standard technique (similar to Z-order or Morton codes) specifically designed to map spatially adjacent 3D points to contiguous memory addresses, thereby improving spatial locality and reducing cache misses. The evidence supports the mechanism (interleaving bits to generate memory addresses) and the goal (reducing cache misses).
